title: [WT-01] Daemon: settings.worktreeMode and the attempt workspace contract
description:
Plan against docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §7.1, §7.2, §1.1, §1.8 and §2.7 (target rule).

Objective: give the daemon the worktree-mode contract every wrapper slice builds on. The mode is pinned per attempt at claim time, so no task switches mode mid-flight.

Deliverable:
- ProjectSettings.worktreeMode: 'off' | 'on' in types/schema.ts, validated in state/validators.ts (anything else is rejected like any bad setting).
- An exported resolveWorktreeMode(settings) in state/validators.ts. It is the ONE place the default lives; the default is 'off' (WT-19 flips it).
- ExecutionAttempt.workspaceMode: 'shared' | 'worktree'.
- claimNextTask.ts sets workspaceMode from resolveWorktreeMode. In worktree mode it sets workspace = <projectPath>/.worktrees/<taskId> (today it is always state.projectPath), and the claim response carries workspace: { mode, path, branch, target }.
  - Worktree: branch = moe/task/<taskId>; target = settings.consolidationBranch when it is a literal name (no *, ? or [), else 'main'.
  - Shared: { mode: 'shared', path: projectPath }, with branch and target null.

NOT in scope: get_context exposure and complete_task branch policy (WT-02); finalize_attempt (WT-03); any wrapper change; flipping the default (WT-19); docs (WT-17).

Verification: cd packages/moe-daemon && npm run build && npx vitest run src/state/validators.test.ts src/tools/claimNextTask.test.ts src/tools/claimNextTask.contract.test.ts
definitionOfDone: state/validators.test.ts: worktreeMode accepts 'off' and 'on' and rejects any other value; resolveWorktreeMode returns 'off' for absent settings.

claimNextTask.test.ts: with worktreeMode 'on' the attempt records workspaceMode 'worktree' and workspace <projectPath>/.worktrees/<taskId>, and the claim response carries workspace {mode:'worktree', path, branch:'moe/task/<taskId>', target}.
claimNextTask.test.ts: with the setting absent or 'off' the attempt records workspaceMode 'shared' and workspace = projectPath, as today.
A test covers the target rule: literal consolidationBranch is used as is, a glob pattern or an unset value yields 'main'.
The verification command in the description exits 0.

implementationPlan.description:
Settings contract: types, validation and the three resolvers, with their unit tests (DoD 1, DoD 4).

Before editing: types/schema.ts is also declared by a dormant peer; see planningNotes.risks (contested paths).

types/schema.ts:
- Add `export type WorktreeMode = 'off' | 'on';` and `export type ExecutionWorkspaceMode = 'shared' | 'worktree';`.
- Add `export interface AttemptWorkspace { mode: ExecutionWorkspaceMode; path: string; branch: string | null; target: string | null }`. It is the `workspace` object claim_next_task returns now and get_context returns in WT-02; branch and target are null in shared mode.
- ProjectSettings: add `worktreeMode?: WorktreeMode;` next to consolidationBranch. Doc comment: 'on' runs each new WORKING claim's attempt in its own git worktree (<projectPath>/.worktrees/<taskId> on moe/task/<taskId>). An absent key means 'off'; resolveWorktreeMode is the only place that default lives, and WT-19 flips it. The setting is read once per attempt at claim time and pinned on ExecutionAttempt.workspaceMode. Any other value is refused.
- ExecutionAttempt: add `workspaceMode?: ExecutionWorkspaceMode;` right after `workspace`. Doc comment: set once by the claim; 'worktree' means `workspace` is the task's worktree. The field is absent on records opened before it existed, and those read as 'shared'. It is optional on purpose: no migration and no schemaVersion bump, like the other additive attempt fields.

state/validators.ts:
- Add 'worktreeMode' to validateSettingsUpdate's rejectUnknownFields allowlist. The file header warns that a field missing from the allowlist is silently dropped.
- Validate it with `if (input.worktreeMode !== undefined) next.worktreeMode = validateEnumValue(input.worktreeMode, 'worktreeMode', WORKTREE_MODES);` using a module const `WORKTREE_MODES: readonly WorktreeMode[] = ['off', 'on']`. Store the value as supplied; an omitted key stays omitted.
- `export function resolveWorktreeMode(settings?: { worktreeMode?: unknown } | null): WorktreeMode`:
  - undefined settings or an undefined key → 'off';
  - 'off' or 'on' → itself;
  - any other stored value, null included → throw invalidInput('worktreeMode', 'must be one of: off, on'). Reusing validateEnumValue gives exactly this message.
  This is the resolveExecutionProfile convention: a malformed stored setting is refused, never read as the default.
- `export function resolveWorktreeTarget(settings?: { consolidationBranch?: unknown } | null): string`. It returns the trimmed consolidationBranch when that is a non-empty string containing no '*', '?' or '[' (design §2.7), else 'main'. It never throws: a non-string from a hand-edited project.json reads as unset, the same type guard completeTask.checkBranchPolicy uses.
- `export function resolveAttemptWorkspace(attempt: Pick<ExecutionAttempt, 'taskId' | 'workspace' | 'workspaceMode'>, settings?: { consolidationBranch?: unknown } | null): AttemptWorkspace`:
  - attempt.workspaceMode === 'worktree' → { mode: 'worktree', path: attempt.workspace, branch: `moe/task/${attempt.taskId}`, target: resolveWorktreeTarget(settings) };
  - anything else (absent on older records, or unrecognised) → { mode: 'shared', path: attempt.workspace, branch: null, target: null }.
  The mode and path come from the attempt, because they are pinned; the target comes from live settings. It never throws, because the claim calls it after its writes.
- Keep the const and the three functions in one small block with a short comment that cites epic-dce3a64f §7.1/§2.7. Add one sentence to the file header naming these resolve* helpers as a third family beside validate*/sanitize*.

Error handling in this step:
- A bad worktreeMode on update throws INVALID_INPUT from validateSettingsUpdate before updateSettings persists anything.
- A malformed stored value throws INVALID_INPUT from resolveWorktreeMode.
- resolveWorktreeTarget and resolveAttemptWorkspace are total: garbage input yields 'main' or shared, never an exception.

state/validators.test.ts: add a new describe('worktree mode'), reusing the file's project() helper. Use toEqual on whole values; no truthiness checks.
- validateSettingsUpdate:
  - accepts 'off' and 'on' (next.worktreeMode equals the input);
  - an unrelated update leaves the key absent;
  - rejects each of 'yes', 'ON', ' on', '', true, 1, null and {} with a message containing 'worktreeMode' and 'must be one of: off, on' (DoD 1).
- resolveWorktreeMode:
  - undefined, null and {} → 'off' (absent settings, DoD 1);
  - { worktreeMode: 'off' } → 'off' and { worktreeMode: 'on' } → 'on';
  - stored 'yes', null and 1 → throw, with error code INVALID_INPUT and the message naming worktreeMode.
- resolveWorktreeTarget (DoD 4):
  - 'main' → 'main'; 'moe/work-2026-10-24' → itself; '  release/v2  ' → 'release/v2';
  - 'moe/work-*', 'rel?ase' and 'feat[0-9]' → 'main';
  - '', '   ', a missing key, undefined settings and 42 → 'main'.
- resolveAttemptWorkspace:
  - a worktree attempt → the full object, with branch 'moe/task/<taskId>' and the resolved target;
  - a shared attempt and an attempt with no workspaceMode → shared, with null branch and target;
  - an unrecognised workspaceMode → shared.
implementationPlan.note: Added the three exported workspace types, optional settings/attempt fields, allowlisted setting validation, and the three resolver exports. Both contested peers confirmed WORKING-unassigned; all seven scope paths were initially clean; unrelated dirty paths left untouched. Native Linux snapshot with matching-lock hardlinked dependencies: validators RED 35 failed/35 passed, GREEN 70 passed. Corrected new test expectations to existing MoeError numeric code/message format, retaining exact INVALID_INPUT and worktreeMode checks. Full named gate remains step 3.

implementationPlan.description:
Pin the mode on the attempt at claim time and return `workspace`, with the claim tests (DoD 2, DoD 3, DoD 4 wiring).

Before editing: tools/claimNextTask.ts is also declared by a dormant peer; see planningNotes.risks.

state/attemptStore.ts:
- OpenAttemptParams gains an optional `workspaceMode?: ExecutionWorkspaceMode`. It is internal, derived by the claim path, never an MCP argument.
- Validate it like the other params: when supplied it must be 'shared' or 'worktree', else throw invalidInput('workspaceMode', ...) before anything is allocated or written.
- openAttempt builds its record from an explicit field list, so without this edit the field is silently dropped. Write it immediately after `workspace` with a conditional spread. Omitted means no key, the legacy shape, so attemptStore.test.ts LEGACY_KEYS stays green. A repair (existing id) still adopts nothing.

tools/claimNextTask.ts, openClaimAttempt:
- Only the fresh and successor arms derive anything. The own-seat resume returns the adopted attempt before any derivation and keeps its mode; that early return IS the pin. Extend the comment that says the resume keeps its original snapshot to also cover workspaceMode/workspace.
- `const workspaceMode: ExecutionWorkspaceMode = task.status === 'WORKING' && resolveWorktreeMode(state.project?.settings) === 'on' ? 'worktree' : 'shared';`
  - Only a WORKING claim runs in a worktree (design §1.3). PLANNING (architect) and REVIEW (QA) attempts stay 'shared' at projectPath even when the setting is on.
  - The status test goes first, so a malformed setting refuses only WORKING claims.
- `workspace` = workspaceMode === 'worktree' ? path.join(state.projectPath, '.worktrees', validateEntityId(taskId, 'taskId')) : state.projectPath.
  - Import `path from 'path'`, validateEntityId from '../util/sanitize.js', and resolveWorktreeMode/resolveAttemptWorkspace from '../state/validators.js'. That import adds no cycle.
  - The id check stops a hand-edited task id from building a path outside .worktrees/.
- Pass workspaceMode in the openAttempt params, and replace the stale "no per-attempt workspace is invented" comment.
- Response: beside attemptId/generation, add `workspace: resolveAttemptWorkspace(claimedAttempt, state.project?.settings)`.
  - It is present whenever attemptId is (both modes) and absent when no worker is named.
  - The hasNext:false and alreadyAssigned replies stay unchanged; the wrapper's resume path reads the workspace from get_context (WT-02).

Error handling in this step:
- A malformed stored worktreeMode, or a task id that fails validateEntityId, throws INVALID_INPUT while the openAttempt params are built.
- The caller's existing catch (handBackUnrecordedClaim) then clears the assignment, so the WORKING claim fails with nothing assigned, no attempt and no worker record. This is the same path a deriveAttemptPolicySnapshot failure takes today.
- openAttempt refuses an unrecognised workspaceMode before writing.
- The response builder cannot throw.

claimNextTask.test.ts: add a new describe('moe.claim_next_task — worktree workspace').
- Use ToolTestHarness, and after h.state.load() call `await h.state.updateSettings({...})`. That goes through validateSettingsUpdate, so a missing allowlist entry fails here too.
- Build every expected worktree path with path.join(h.state.projectPath, '.worktrees', <id>), never a '/' literal, so the tests pass on Windows.
- Cases:
  1. (DoD 2) 'on' plus a WORKING claim. The attempt in memory (listAttempts) AND on disk (.moe/attempts/<id>.json) has workspaceMode 'worktree' and workspace = the joined path. result.workspace toEqual { mode: 'worktree', path, branch: 'moe/task/task-1', target: 'main' }.
  2. (DoD 3) The setting absent, and set to 'off': the attempt has workspaceMode 'shared' and workspace h.state.projectPath. result.workspace toEqual { mode: 'shared', path: h.state.projectPath, branch: null, target: null }.
  3. (DoD 4 wiring) 'on' with consolidationBranch 'moe/work-2026-10-24' → target 'moe/work-2026-10-24'; with 'moe/work-*' → 'main'.
  4. 'on' plus a PLANNING claim (statuses ['PLANNING']) and a REVIEW claim (['REVIEW']) both record 'shared' at projectPath and return mode 'shared'.
  5. Pin: claim under 'on' (worktree), then set 'off'. The own-seat re-claim by taskId returns the same attemptId, an identical workspace object and unchanged attempt-file bytes. Then release (releaseTaskTool) and claim again: generation 2 records 'shared'.
  6. Error handling: set `(h.state.project!.settings as Record<string, unknown>).worktreeMode = 'yes'`. The WORKING claim rejects with INVALID_INPUT naming worktreeMode, the task is unassigned and listAttempts is empty.
  7. Injection: a claim carrying workspaceMode 'worktree' and workspace '/elsewhere' as args, under the default setting, still records 'shared' at projectPath. The tool's inputSchema properties contain neither key.
  8. openAttempt with workspaceMode 'bogus' rejects with INVALID_INPUT and writes no attempt file.
- In the existing 'opens no attempt on the alreadyAssigned refusal' test, add `expect(refused).not.toHaveProperty('workspace')`.

Three existing assertions pin today's shapes. A prototype run confirmed that these 5 tests fail, and no others:
- claimNextTask.test.ts, 'writes a claim that sends no identity byte for byte as before': insert `workspaceMode: 'shared'` right after `workspace` in the expected JSON.
- claimNextTask.test.ts, 'opens one running generation-1 attempt…': add workspaceMode 'shared' to its toMatchObject and fix its comment about the workspace.
- claimNextTask.contract.test.ts: add 'workspace' to both Object.keys(result) lists ('keeps claim response lean…' and the C5 it.each), and extend the comment above the first list to say the workspace is where the attempt runs (WT-01).
implementationPlan.note: Pinned daemon-derived workspaceMode/workspace for fresh/successor claims; adopted attempts bypass derivation. Added workspace response only with attempt identity. Covered persisted bytes, default/off, literal/glob target, PLANNING/REVIEW including malformed settings, resume/new generation, failure compensation, ignored injection, invalid open mode, repair/phase preservation and absent-workspace refusals. Rechecked contested claim peer idle before editing. RED: 17 failures/111 passes (after correcting test syntax); GREEN: claim+contract+attemptStore 200/200. Fixed new no-write tests to assert the attempts directory is absent, rather than assuming an empty existing directory. Also clarified validators header (step-1 file) and identity comment; no behavior scope expansion.

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review of this task's own diff, as the final step. Load the adversarial-self-review skill. Check each item:
1. 'worktreeMode' is in validateSettingsUpdate's allowlist, and updateSettings round-trips it.
2. No resume, repair or reattach path re-derives the mode: only the fresh and successor arms of openClaimAttempt read settings, and an adopted attempt's workspace/workspaceMode bytes never change.
3. WORKING-only: with the setting on, PLANNING and REVIEW claims record 'shared'.
4. Error handling: resolveWorktreeTarget and resolveAttemptWorkspace never throw on garbage (null settings, number, array, object). The response is built after the claim's writes, so a throw there would misreport a claim that already happened.
5. A malformed setting refuses only WORKING claims, and the hand-back leaves no assignment, no attempt and no new worker record.
6. The worktree path uses path.join and validateEntityId, and the tests build expected paths with path.join, so they pass on Windows.
7. Rail 4: in shared mode the attempt workspace is still state.projectPath. The only shared-mode changes are the new workspaceMode:'shared' key and the response's workspace object.
8. No caller argument reaches workspaceMode or workspace.
9. Everything still runs inside runExclusive, with no new subprocess or IO under the mutex beyond the existing attempt write.
10. Every doc comment you added matches the code.

If this review changes any byte, re-run step 3's command and submit that last fresh output as the complete_task evidence. In complete_task's summary, list every exported name you added.

comments.content:
Retraction of my comment 13abdc64. Keep your planned contract (Serena decision-worktree-attempt-workspace-contract):

- Only a WORKING claim gets workspaceMode 'worktree' with W.
- PLANNING and REVIEW claims stay 'shared' at projectPath, with null branch and target, even when the setting is on.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: settings.worktreeMode ('off' | 'on'; absent means 'off', resolved only by resolveWorktreeMode) decides where each NEW worker attempt runs. A WORKING claim opened while it resolves to 'on' records workspaceMode 'worktree' and workspace = path.join(projectPath, '.worktrees', taskId). Every other claim records workspaceMode 'shared' and workspace = projectPath, as today: the setting off or absent, or any PLANNING or REVIEW claim. The mode is pinned on the attempt, and an own-seat resume keeps it. Every claim response that carries attemptId also carries workspace {mode, path, branch, target}, built from the attempt by resolveAttemptWorkspace. In worktree mode, branch is 'moe/task/<taskId>' and target is the trimmed literal consolidationBranch, else 'main'. In shared mode, branch and target are null.
acceptanceCriteria: validateSettingsUpdate accepts worktreeMode 'off' and 'on' and rejects any other value with 'worktreeMode must be one of: off, on'.
resolveWorktreeMode returns 'off' for absent settings or key and throws INVALID_INPUT for any other stored value.

With 'on', a WORKING claim's attempt (in memory and on disk) has workspaceMode 'worktree' and workspace <projectPath>/.worktrees/<taskId>, and the response has workspace {mode:'worktree', path, branch:'moe/task/<taskId>', target}.
With the setting absent or 'off', the attempt has workspaceMode 'shared' and workspace = projectPath, and the response has workspace {mode:'shared', path: projectPath, branch:null, target:null}.
Target rule: a literal consolidationBranch is used as is (trimmed); a value containing *, ? or [, an empty value or an unset value yields 'main'.
With 'on', PLANNING and REVIEW claims record and return 'shared'.
An own-seat resume after the setting flips returns the same attempt with an unchanged workspace.
invariants: workspaceMode and workspace derive from daemon state only; no claim argument reaches them.
An attempt's workspaceMode and workspace never change after open.
The worktree path is built only from a task id that passes validateEntityId, so it cannot leave .worktrees/.
Shared mode is unchanged except for the added workspaceMode:'shared' attempt key and the response's workspace object (epic rail 4).
compatibility: Attempt records without workspaceMode, written before this change, read as 'shared'. No migration and no schemaVersion bump.
openAttempt without workspaceMode still writes the legacy shape.
The hasNext:false and alreadyAssigned claim replies are unchanged.
Today's sh/ps1 wrappers read named keys only, so the extra claim key and attempt key are ignored.

state/validators.ts: the 'worktreeMode' allowlist entry and validation, plus resolveWorktreeMode, resolveWorktreeTarget, resolveAttemptWorkspace
tools/claimNextTask.ts: openClaimAttempt's workspace derivation and the response's workspace
reuse: validateEnumValue for the setting and the resolver's refusal message
validateEntityId (util/sanitize.ts) for the worktree path segment
the undefined-to-default / malformed-to-INVALID_INPUT convention of resolveExecutionProfile
the existing handBackUnrecordedClaim path for a refused derivation
sourceAssumptions: state/attemptStore.ts openAttempt builds its record from an explicit field list.
tools/claimNextTask.ts openClaimAttempt returns an own-seat resume before deriving anything.
state/validators.ts validateSettingsUpdate allowlists fields through rejectUnknownFields.
tools/claimNextTask.contract.test.ts pins Object.keys(result) at two sites; tools/claimNextTask.test.ts pins exact attempt bytes in the runner-identity describe.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Each alternative, and why it was rejected:
- Put the shared helpers in tools/claimNextTask.ts and export them. getContext.ts (WT-02) imports only state/, util/, delivery/ and context/ modules, never another tool. So resolveWorktreeTarget and resolveAttemptWorkspace live in state/validators.ts beside the mandated resolveWorktreeMode, which also gives WT-02 and WT-16 one import site.
- Give every claim a worktree when the setting is on. Design §1.3 says only a worker seat holding a WORKING claim gets W, and architect, QA and governor seats stay in the control checkout. An architect or QA attempt recorded as 'worktree' would describe a W nobody creates, and the wrappers take the mode from the claim (§7.1).
- Have resolveWorktreeMode fall back to 'off' on a malformed stored value. resolveExecutionProfile and resolveDeliveryPolicy refuse malformed stored settings instead of reading them as the default. Also, a silent 'off' after the flip runbook set consolidationBranch 'main' would put shared-mode seats on the main-direct path. So it throws INVALID_INPUT, and the status-first ordering limits the damage to WORKING claims.
- Reuse cachedPlanRef's literal-branch regex for the target. It is stricter than §2.7's rule and DoD 4 (no * ? [) and would silently send some valid literal names to main.
- Pin the target on the attempt as well. Neither the DoD nor §1.8 asks for it, and the flip is stop-the-world (§7.4), so a live read is enough.
- Split the task to stay within 5 files. The total is about 150-200 net LOC, and DoD 2-4 need the setting, the attempt field and the response together, so the 7-file warning is expected. Two files beyond the design's list are required:
  - attemptStore.ts, because openAttempt drops unknown fields;
  - claimNextTask.contract.test.ts, because it pins Object.keys(result).
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Facts the plan relies on:
- state/attemptStore.ts openAttempt builds the record from a fixed field list: id, taskId, workerId, runnerId, generation, workspace, phase, startedAt and lastPhaseAt, plus conditional processStartedAt, host and executionPolicySnapshot. setAttemptPhase and detached() spread `...attempt`, and loadEntities reads raw JSON, so the new key survives phase changes and restarts with no further edits.
- tools/claimNextTask.ts openClaimAttempt returns an own-seat resume (`resumed && resumingOwnSeat && resumed.workerId === workerId`) before anything is derived; that is the pin. Every other arm builds params, so the new derivation sits next to deriveAttemptPolicySnapshot and fails the same way: a throw leads to handBackUnrecordedClaim in the caller.
- Only claimNextTask.ts calls openAttempt (outside tests).
- The claim response spreads `{attemptId, generation}` only when claimedAttempt is set, and the new `workspace` joins that spread.
- validators.ts already imports validateEntityId (util/sanitize.ts: ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$, at most 128) and validateEnumValue, whose message is 'must be one of: off, on'.
- The tests can call state.updateSettings, which runs validateSettingsUpdate.
- The wrappers (sh python and ps1 ConvertFrom-Json) read named keys from claim JSON and attempt files, so the extra keys are ignored.
- tsconfig excludes *.test.ts, so `npm run build` type-checks only the source.
- A scratch prototype of the whole change passed tsc --noEmit. Its new behaviors passed, and exactly 5 existing tests failed, all of them the shape pins step 2 names: 4 in the contract test, 1 bytes test.
planningNotes.risks:
Contested paths. Two dormant peers declare files this plan edits, both WORKING-unassigned, dependency-gated, with no commits or dirty bytes at planning time:
- types/schema.ts: task-724e31fadd3e4f5cb137abe9e4147f11;
- tools/claimNextTask.ts: task-af83018e892149a1a18cd6a946edeba5.
Under the default attribution.contested 'skip-untouched', such a path lands when this session's supported editing tool wrote it, or when it was clean at this session's pre-flight and every contesting task is idle. Before editing, run moe.get_commit_scope {taskId, phase:'postflight'} (or list_tasks) to confirm both peers are still seatless. If either has a live seat, coordinate with it in chat first. A seat whose edits leave no wrapper-observed witness (codex, gemini, grok) then calls report_blocked with blockedOnTaskIds set to that peer instead of editing. Never weaken the policy or hand-land the path.

Other risks:
- Exact-bytes test: the key order in the expected JSON must match the record, so put workspaceMode right after workspace.
- Windows: expected worktree paths must use path.join.
